question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}2 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\\5 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\pi}{3}\\0\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=2 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}$ and $y(u,v)=5 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}&- 5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(- 5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\right)-\left(- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(5 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\right)\\&=10 \sin{\left(u + v \right)} \cos{\left(u - v \right)}-\left(- 10 \sin{\left(u + v \right)} \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\right)\\&=20 \sin{\left(u + v \right)} \cos{\left(u - v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\pi}{3}\\0\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(\frac{\pi}{3},0)}=20 \sin{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) + \left(0\right) \right)} \cos{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) - \left(0\right) \right)}=5 \sqrt{3}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}u v\\\frac{4 v}{u}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=u v$ and $y(u,v)=\frac{4 v}{u}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=v&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=u\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=- \frac{4 v}{u^{2}}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\frac{4}{u}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}v&u\\- \frac{4 v}{u^{2}}&\frac{4}{u}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(v\right)\cdot\left(\frac{4}{u}\right)-\left(u\right)\cdot\left(- \frac{4 v}{u^{2}}\right)\\&=\frac{8 v}{u}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(2,-1)}=\frac{8 \left(-1\right)}{\left(2\right)}=-4.
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}\cos{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}\\\sin{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\pi}{6}\\\frac{\pi}{6}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=\cos{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}$ and $y(u,v)=\sin{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=2 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 3 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}&- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}\\2 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}&- 3 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(- 3 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}\right)-\left(- 2 \sin{\left(2 u + 2 v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(2 \cos{\left(2 u - 3 v \right)}\right)\\&=5 \left(\sin{\left(5 v \right)} + \sin{\left(4 u - v \right)}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\pi}{6}\\\frac{\pi}{6}\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{6})}=5 \sin{\left(5 \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \right)} + 5 \sin{\left(4 \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) - \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \right)}=\frac{15}{2}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}e^{4 u - 3 v}\\\log{\left(u v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=e^{4 u - 3 v}$ and $y(u,v)=\log{\left(u v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=4 e^{4 u - 3 v}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- 3 e^{4 u - 3 v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=\frac{1}{u}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\frac{1}{v}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}4 e^{4 u - 3 v}&- 3 e^{4 u - 3 v}\\\frac{1}{u}&\frac{1}{v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(4 e^{4 u - 3 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)-\left(- 3 e^{4 u - 3 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{u}\right)\\&=\frac{\left(4 u + 3 v\right) e^{4 u} e^{- 3 v}}{u v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(3,4)}=\frac{\left(4 \left(3\right) + 3 \left(4\right)\right) e^{4 \left(3\right)} e^{- 3 \left(4\right)}}{\left(3\right) \left(4\right)}=2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 \left(u + v\right)^{3}\\3 \left(u - v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\-2\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=3 \left(u + v\right)^{3}$ and $y(u,v)=3 \left(u - v\right)^{3}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}&9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\\9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}&- 9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(- 9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\right)-\left(9 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(9 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\right)\\&=- 162 \left(u - v\right)^{2} \left(u + v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\-2\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(1,-2)}=- 162 \left(\left(1\right) - \left(-2\right)\right)^{2} \left(\left(1\right) + \left(-2\right)\right)^{2}=-1458.
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}2 \left(u + v\right)^{3}\\3 \left(u - v\right)^{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=2 \left(u + v\right)^{3}$ and $y(u,v)=3 \left(u - v\right)^{2}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6 u - 6 v&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 6 u + 6 v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left|\begin{matrix}6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}&6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\\6 u - 6 v&- 6 u + 6 v\end{matrix}\right|\\&=\left(6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(- 6 u + 6 v\right)-\left(6 \left(u + v\right)^{2}\right)\cdot\left(6 u - 6 v\right)\\&=- 72 \left(u - v\right) \left(u + v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\end{bmatrix},$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(2,-1)}=- 72 \left(\left(2\right) - \left(-1\right)\right) \left(\left(2\right) + \left(-1\right)\right)^{2}=-216.
$$
